packet: author-packet — offline authoring, MiniMax packet discipline (reasons first, hard token cap, graveyard on failure). Format per coach-player docs/OVERSEER-NUMBERS.md §9: packet cap 4k tokens in / 2k out, enforced before the call; in this M1 proof NO model call was made — the packet is the artefact the call would have consumed, authored by hand against it, so the discipline is exercised end to end with the spend at zero.

why: The overseer's misfit path and its keyhole both need a held state, and M0 improvised it: zeroInput() during misfit-pause / hold, with no tile accountable for the boat during the pause and no label ever written for the situation (overseer.js M0, phases 'hold' / 'misfit-pause').

MiniMax §3.5 names the missing piece: a reflex hold-station tile for the keyhole-with-no-human case — 'no decision, no confidence'. The library had no claimant for the registry intention 'hold-station' (registry.js before this tile) — a structural gap, the exact class M1's registry exists to expose.

Every work tile's back phase re-implements drone recovery privately (hunt-the-pot, wreck-look, work-the-shoal). A standalone recovery-and-hold claimant gives the coach (and later, the overseer itself) one named choice — 'bring her in and hold' — instead of three private copies of the idea.

topRejectedAlternatives.candidate: extend make-way with a zero-length target (hold = go nowhere)
topRejectedAlternatives.rejected: make-way's arrival/timeout semantics price a transit; a zero-length leg 'arrives' instantly and teaches the label store that holding is a completed transit. The hold is its own intention.

topRejectedAlternatives.candidate: leave the improvisation (zeroInput in the overseer)
topRejectedAlternatives.rejected: unaccountable and unlabelled: no costs priced, no recovery if the drone is out when the pause begins, no graduation path. The design's whole point is that behaviour lives in tiles.
recovery is this tile's first phase; a recovery-only tile ends with the drone aboard and the boat drifting — the hold is the intention a coach actually holds. One tile, both halves, priced as one.

section2_situation_digest.situationClass: hold-station (intention with no claimant — structural gap)
section2_situation_digest.recurrence: every misfit pause, every keyhole, every coach 'hold on' — the most frequent unclaimed situation in the M0 traces (each always-0.3 control run logs hold-station story lines with no tile behind them)
section2_situation_digest.host: Shoalwater, F/V Eileen + drone, real pack
railsThatBind: drone recovery uses the game's own rule (within 15 m at any height; the tile switches at < 12 m, via the shared tryRecover)
failure flies home first: the recovery phase precedes any failure verdict; the tile settles 'failed' only after a bounded 240 s recovery attempt
the reserve third is never spent by this tile (no objective flight; recovery is direct)

section3_projected_questions: over-001 (when does the overseer get to say none-of-these) — this tile is the floor under that verdict
over-006 (graduation measured on coach presses) — the coach order 'hold station' resolves to this tile through the interpreter
over-008 (tile health grace) — a reflex tile is exempt by design: no confidence, no health scoring, priced watch instead
section1_reasons_first.section4_sheet_excerpt: Avatar sheet dials at authoring time: caution mid, boldness mid — a reflex tile expresses neither; it is the hand-steering layer of the stack, useful when everything above it has nothing to say.

section5_tile_spec.premise: Bring everything to a safe held state — the drone home aboard, the boat on station — and watch for a spell.
section5_tile_spec.precondition: { ok: true } always — declared exception: a reflex that can decline is not a reflex. Fail-closed still binds its navigation (adapter NaN reads as shoal to the keel cap).
phases: recover (drone home aboard; bounded 240 s; failure settles only after the bound)
hold (station-keep on the anchor point: drift > 25 m walked back at creep 1.3 keel-capped; inside it, engines easy)

exits.resourceGuard: none spendable — the tile spends time only

section5_tile_spec.judgeHeuristic: exposure-based: drone out + battery < 0.5 -> 0.90; drone out -> 0.75; all aboard -> 0.55 (judges.js)

section6_token_accounting.spend: 0 — no model call was made in this proof; the packet was authored by the session against the format, and the tile verified by the harness bar that exists today (M1). The accounting exists so that when a pulse IS spent, this file is what it buys.

verification.bar: the statistical bar that exists today (M1): harness-style runs across 3 tides (tools/m1-test.mjs) + the six standing suites unaffected
verification.results: hold-station at tides -1.5 / +1.4 / +4.0 from a drone-out start: drone recovered aboard, watch held inside 25 m of the anchor, 'done', zero hull hits, reserve unspent — see tools/m1-test.mjs output
verification.contract: checked line by line against coach-player docs/TILE-CONTRACT.md (declare / require / bounded phases with an exit each / decline stance declared / outcome + evidence / judge heuristic / rails)

section1_reasons_first.provenance: authored pulse (offline, M1) — first authored tile in the library; enters on probation per the contract (MM: demote on an early abort; CL: 5 live uses, >= 4 successes, 0 takeovers to earn the library proper). Owner rules on graduation.
